Precision is counted per finding (defect-class findings that match an issue / all defect-class findings); recall is counted per issue (issues matched / 17).
notes: Why 14 correct findings can sit beside 17 issues found: the answer key has 14 defect-class issues and 3 others (quality, maintainability, standards). Found counts issues of every category. Correct counts findings of the defect classes only. They are separate counts, so Correct + Missed need not equal the number of issues.
Rule-detectable recall covers 16 issues. Semantic recall covers 1, so it can only be 0 or 1 in a run.
F1 here mixes defect precision and issue recall, which have different denominators. Treat it as a summary of this benchmark, not a standard F1.
Precision is N/A, not 1.0, when a configuration reports no defect findings at all.

tables.about: Self-supervised from the AST call graph: for each function, the relevant chunks are those containing the functions it calls; the query is the function's own chunk.

conditions.review-time retrieval: top_k = 6 similar chunks + guideline_k = 2 guideline chunks per review unit

observations: RAG (bm25) has a higher Recall@10 than random (0.362 vs 0.007).
RAG (hashing) has a higher Recall@10 than random (0.382 vs 0.007).
notes: This measures whether retrieval finds a function's call-graph neighbours. It does not measure final review accuracy, and its effect on reviews needs Static + LLM vs Static + LLM + RAG on identical samples.
5 retrieval runs are saved, on 138, 277, 316, 381, 711 queries. The repository grew between them, so they are not comparable. This table shows the latest.
Recall@3 and the other Hit@k cut-offs are in run 20261110T114239Z_retrieval_src.

Precision is counted per finding (defect-class findings that match an issue / all defect-class findings); recall is counted per issue (issues matched / 17).
notes: Why 14 correct findings can sit beside 17 issues found: the answer key has 14 defect-class issues and 3 others (quality, maintainability, standards). Found counts issues of every category. Correct counts findings of the defect classes only. They are separate counts, so Correct + Missed need not equal the number of issues.
Rule-detectable recall covers 16 issues. Semantic recall covers 1, so it can only be 0 or 1 in a run.
F1 here mixes defect precision and issue recall, which have different denominators. Treat it as a summary of this benchmark, not a standard F1.
Precision is N/A, not 1.0, when a configuration reports no defect findings at all.
Run: python -m marl_agents.cli eval ablation --benchmark planted --config configs/ollama.yaml --provider ollama
tables.warning: Local development runs. They are reported apart and are not comparable with, or merged into, the Gemini results above. Small benchmark: 17 issues written by the project team. It is a regression check, and a score of 1.000 is not evidence of 100% bug detection in real code.

definitions.name: Issue recall
definitions.definition: Labelled issues found / all labelled issues (any category).

definitions.name: Defect precision
definitions.definition: Correct defect findings / all defect findings. Style and documentation findings are not in the answer key, so they are not counted.

definitions.name: F1 (mixed basis)
definitions.definition: Harmonic mean of defect precision and issue recall. The two have different denominators, so this is not a standard F1.

definitions.name: ROC-AUC
definitions.definition: Probability that a randomly chosen positive case is scored above a randomly chosen negative one (Mann-Whitney U; ties count 1/2): ranking quality across all thresholds. 0.5 = chance.

definitions.name: BLEU-4
definitions.definition: Smoothed sentence BLEU-4 (Lin & Och 2004 +1 smoothing for n >= 2), averaged over samples, x100 (CodeReviewer convention).

definitions.name: ROUGE-L
definitions.definition: Longest-common-subsequence F1 of word tokens, averaged over samples, x100.

definitions.name: chrF
definitions.definition: Character 1-6-gram F-score (beta = 2, Popovic 2015), averaged over samples, x100.

definitions.name: Coverage
definitions.definition: Share of diffs for which the agent produced a comment.

definitions.name: Recall@10
definitions.definition: Share of a query's relevant chunks (its callees in the AST call graph) found in the top 10 retrieved; averaged over queries.

definitions.name: MRR
definitions.definition: Mean over queries of 1 / rank of the first relevant chunk.

definitions.name: Precision@Top10%
definitions.definition: Of the 10% of hunks ranked riskiest, the share a human reviewer commented on.

definitions.name: Rating
definitions.definition: Mean 1-5 rating by the LLM judge (supplementary).

scope: Agent-level benchmark evaluation of the Code Review Agent on its own. These numbers are not system-level results of the five-agent platform (SWE-bench Lite resolve rate), which is not built yet.
Configuration D (Static + LLM + RAG) is the shipped Code Review Agent; A-C are ablations that switch one component off.

Every value comes from a saved run in experiments/results/ (run ids are listed per row). A configuration without a valid run is N/A with the command that produces it. Runs made with the offline mock LLM test the pipeline and are never shown as results.

limitations: Planted benchmark: 17 issues written by the project team, and only one needs semantic reasoning. It is a regression check, not evidence of real-world accuracy.
CodeReviewer labels record whether a human commented, which is a proxy for 'needs attention', not a defect label.
Every LLM comparison so far uses Groq-hosted models. No Gemini result exists for detection or comment quality, and results from different models must not be combined.
The Gemini free tier allows 20 requests per day per model, so larger comparisons run over several days with --reuse-llm-cache. Their quality metrics compare; their times do not.
All runs come from an uncommitted working tree, so none can be traced to a commit.
This evaluates the Code Review Agent alone, not the five-agent platform.
findings: Static analysis alone barely predicts where humans comment: ROC-AUC 0.539 with cross-hunk rules removed, 0.417 raw (n = 4195).

The fine-tuned classifier ranks human-commented changes better than its baselines: ROC-AUC 0.723 (95% CI 0.699-0.748), against TF-IDF 0.645 and size 0.635 (n = 1771). This is a proxy label, and review quality was not measured.
Risk model v2 does not beat the size baseline: ROC-AUC 0.644 against 0.651.
Retrieval finds call-graph neighbours far better than random: Recall@10 0.362 against 0.007. That is retrieval quality, not review accuracy.
